title: Resolve §6.3.2's portrait-region ambiguity and correct its table
description:
plan.md ref: §6.3.2. The section says to expose a portrait/landscape setting and then says
"this is coaching, not configuration" — a reader cannot tell what the sender should
do. The two routes also compose badly: a landscape receiver plus a portrait sender
region gives ~7 camera px/module, 3x more than needed, at half the tiles that
geometry could carry. No rule is given for choosing. The supporting table is also
arithmetically inconsistent — rows are computed at different screen px/module, and
row 2's verdict inverts under its own arithmetic — and "worth ~4-5x, Measured" is an
inference, not a measurement.

title: Implement G3: bundle-size budget, SRI, no post-install scripts
description:
plan.md ref: §14.5, §13.1. Unimplemented, and the bundle-size number is never given anywhere
including §13.1.

title: F10: Verifiable reproducible build with version footer
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F10, grade M). Entered via the gap round. Scope extended by user: include a semver at the bottom of the page.

Publish a hash of the deployed bundle; the app displays its own version and hash
so a user in a sensitive environment can confirm it matches the audited release.

## Why
The security claim is 'a static page with no network calls can be audited once
and trusted thereafter'. That claim is only real if a user can tell WHICH page
they are running. Without it the audit applies to a version nobody can identify.

## First step
Semver plus short build hash in the page footer, sourced from the build, not
hand-maintained. Cheap, immediately useful, and the anchor everything else hangs
off.

## Then
- Deterministic/reproducible build pipeline so third parties can regenerate the
  published hash
- Publish hashes per release
- Optional in-page 'verify' affordance explaining how to check

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- transmission manifest export (streamId + block hashes)
- published open format spec inviting third-party implementations

## Surviving objection
The audience who would actually verify a hash is small, and static-host deploy
pipelines make byte-reproducibility fiddly. The version footer is worth it
regardless; full reproducibility is the part that needs justifying.

Plan refs: README security claim, docs/notes/concept.md constraint 1. Phase 0
for the footer, later for reproducibility.

title: Add capture-resolution selection to the receiver pipeline
description:
plan.md ref: §6.4. Measured knee: 720p -> 100% erasure (1.5 camera px/module); 1080p best
goodput; 4K zero empty frames but 194 ms decode and 1.1 fps, net worse. §6.4's
pipeline has no resolution-selection step, and getUserMedia defaults are NOT
adequate — a Pixel 6 defaults to 1080 on the SHORT edge.

title: Resolve the resume / compression / T4-reap conflict
description:
plan.md ref: §8.3, D8, T4, E11. §8.3 says "the sender is stateless across restarts by
construction". FALSE with compression on: the wire payload is the compressed staging
file, and CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee across runs, versions or
platforms. E11 reaps staging on startup and T4 requires wiping it for privacy. So
sender restarts -> staging reaped -> re-compress -> different bytes -> different
block boundaries and hashes -> the receiver's bitmap, output and manifest silently
invalid. Either preserve staging across restarts (and amend T4) or forbid resume
with compression on.

title: Declare L a wire constant for wireVersion 1
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, T1, D15, §3.1.1. L is ambiguous between wire constant and session-
negotiable. params.ts hardcodes L=256 and §3.1.1 derives the entire rung ladder from
it, yet §7.2 transmits fragmentLen and T1 bounds-checks it over [1,4096]. A receiver
built to this code cannot decode any stream with L != 256, so T1's range check is
meaningless. RECOMMEND: wire constant; keep the beacon field as a validity check and
reject a mismatch with E-VERSION.

title: Fix the Modulation interface before Phase 2 wires against it
description:
plan.md ref: §6.1, §6.5, review-3 critical #12. §6.5 calls modulation/types.ts "the ONLY
contract above" the swappable layer, and it cannot express the plan's own decisions:
D16 needs 2-4 profiles mixed WITHIN a frame but packetsPerFrame is a scalar and
encodeFrame gets an undifferentiated array; D18b and §11 need per-tile yield and
quality (cameraPxPerModule, E-TORN, E-BLUR) which decodeFrame discards; and
decodeFrame(VideoFrame) contradicts §6.5's mandated non-Chromium fallback, which
produces ImageData. Changing this after Phase 2 wires a receiver is the AR-2/AR-4
pivot class.

title: Phase 2: single-QR optical loop with the real codec
description:
plan.md ref: §17. THE VALIDATION GAP. The codec is tested headlessly (22 tests) and the
channel via the spike rig; THE SEAM BETWEEN THEM IS UNTESTED and no file has ever
moved end to end. Wire src/core into the optical path: file -> toFragments ->
LTEncoder -> tiles -> camera -> GEDecoder -> fromFragments -> hash compare. This
also exercises what the rig fakes — index derivation over a real link, rank
convergence against real erasure, and the short-last-block path (E3a's shared
blockK property is currently never exercised).

title: F3: Aim reticle and distance coach
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F3, grade M).

A document-scanner-style reticle the user aligns the sender's screen into, with
live px/module feedback.

## Why
Defends the 4 px/module cliff -- the highest-impact measured effect in all the
research. Geometry, not software, is the dominant risk: laptop->phone gives
~165 cells across, phone->phone only ~54.

## First step
Overlay the reticle plus a red/amber/green px/module readout driven by QR finder
pattern spacing.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- 'prop your phone up' setup guidance (every published experiment used a stand)
- distance coaching ('move closer' / 'too close to focus')

## Surviving objection
Haptic feedback cannot help on iOS -- no Vibration API in Safari -- so the
visual channel must carry the whole message.

Plan refs: section 7 geometry, D16. Phase 5.

title: Add PacketFlags.Manifest; remove or reserve Repetition
description:
plan.md ref: §7.6, params.ts. PacketFlags.Manifest is named as normative in §7.6 and does
not exist in params.ts. PacketFlags.Repetition exists and is never used (repetition
is derived per-block).

title: Convert RecvSession write sites to positional interface
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Find all write(buf) calls in RecvSession
- Replace each with write(buf, {at}) using tracked position
- Verify all write paths use the new positional interface
- No sequential stream writes remain in RecvSession

## Context
Now that we have the handle and position tracking, convert all actual write sites from stream writes to positional writes with explicit {at} parameter.

title: Specify the mixed-size tile layout algorithm
description:
plan.md ref: D16, §6.3.2. The four rungs are different QR versions (57/81/97/109 modules), so
at a common screen px/module they are physically different-sized tiles. §6.3.2's
table and the spike's 5x3 grid both assume uniform tiles. Simplest rule: allocate
the grid at R1 pitch and let denser rungs occupy an integral number of R1 cells.

title: Add the incremental WASM hasher to §6.5's pins and module tree
description:
plan.md ref: §6.5, §3.3. The mandatory whole-file hash needs an incremental hasher that
appears in neither the dependency-pin table nor the module tree, and is not scoped
by G3 or §14.4 — i.e. a second WASM blob that could lazily fetch from a CDN.

title: Move QR decode into a worker pool
description:
plan.md ref: §6.2, §13.1. Measured decode p50 67-69 ms on a full 1080p frame, single-threaded
on the main thread, gating camera fps at 4.5-6.3. §13.1 budgets <= 60 ms p99 — p50
already exceeds the p99 budget. §6.2 specifies the design (N workers, VideoFrame
must be close()d or the pipeline stalls, drop-don't-queue backpressure); it is
unimplemented and was assigned to no phase. Honour I6b: cap in-flight frames at 4,
since one 1080p RGBA frame is 7.9 MiB.

title: Enhance debug logging for deletion verification
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Add console.log statements showing when deletion starts/completes
- Log streamId and filename for each deletion attempt
- Log deletion errors with enough detail to diagnose issues
- Add timing information (how long deletion took)
- Ensure logs are visible in browser DevTools
- Add structured logs that can be parsed for debugging

## Scope
Enhance the existing logging in export.ts to make deletion more observable and debuggable. The deletion logic exists but logging may need improvement for troubleshooting.

## Dependencies
Depends on: bf-9it9 (integration test)

title: Reconcile §6.5's module tree with the as-built code
description:
plan.md ref: §6.5. Plan says fountain/{lt-encode,ge-decode,degree}.ts and
block/{bitmap,schedule}.ts; built is fountain/{encoder,decoder,prng}.ts and
block/partition.ts. And src/core/params.ts — the most load-bearing file in the repo,
what G7 diffs against, home of the rung table and its import-time guard — IS NOT IN
THE PLAN AT ALL.

title: Publish the e_max completion cliff in §8.1
description:
plan.md ref: §8.1, review-3 critical #5. VERIFIED: a block completes on a pass iff
dwell*(1-e) >= 1+overhead. At dwell 1.6 and the measured +2.97%:
e_max = 1 - 1.03/1.6 = 35.6%. Above that every pass delivers < K independent
packets, the decoder resets, and the next pass starts from rank 0 — the transfer
NEVER FINISHES, at any file size, with the progress bar frozen at zero blocks.
State this explicitly; it is currently implicit in a table.

title: Give the receiver's decoded file a deletion lifecycle (T4b)
description:
plan.md ref: §12 T4, E10, E15. T4's threat covers both ends but its mitigation is sender-only,
so the flagship use case leaves a complete plaintext copy of an SSH key in browser
storage indefinitely. T4's stated test is also unimplementable, since the receiver's
output IS the deliverable. Split into T4a/T4b; specify deletion after a successful
share()/save, startup reap of orphaned outputs, a warning before keeping a partial
artefact, and a user-visible delete control.

title: Add a local-diagnostics rule: never log payload bytes
description:
plan.md ref: §12 T7. T7 forbids NETWORK telemetry and says nothing about local logs.
RecvSession.stats, bf-5vm's stall detector, window.sfStats (which tools/cdp_eval.py
exfiltrates over CDP by design) and §8.2's clipboard repair code could all carry
filenames or payload bytes.

title: Build the stub-camera test tier
description:
plan.md ref: §14.1. The workhorse tier — getUserMedia stubbed with canvas.captureStream(0)
driven by requestFrame(). No flags, frame-exact, deterministic. Required by G1.

title: Implement G2, the no-network assertion
description:
plan.md ref: §14.4. Unimplemented. It MUST exercise a DECODE, because zxing's WASM fetch is
lazy and does not occur until first use — the most likely violation would otherwise
go undetected.

title: Generate test/fixtures/vectors.json — retire AP10
description:
plan.md ref: I3, §14.3, AP10. prng.ts:9 asserts the file pins the wire format; the file does
not exist and test/fixtures/ is empty. AP10 records this in the PAST tense while it
is live in the exact file it names. The PRNG tests assert only same-process
determinism, which a refactor of splitmix32 would satisfy while silently changing
the wire format with all 22 tests green.

title: Run the long-run thermal profile
description:
plan.md ref: R11, D27, §18.2. THE most important unrun measurement. Cool start, recorded
starting temperature, decode continuously, plot decode latency and camera fps
against elapsed time until steady state. Observed so far: 70 C and quiet_therm at
mStatus=1 after 20-30 minutes, against a §1.1 objective of 27 h - 4 days.

title: 41 of 225 tests failing across 5 test files
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 on bench.

npm run test: 5 test files failed, 41 tests failed, 184 passed (225 total).

Baseline before d3f4cbd was 33 failed / 170 passed of 203. The delta is because the stray brace in test/storage.test.ts prevented 22 tests in that file from being collected at all. The 8 additional failures are pre-existing breakage that was never being exercised, not a regression from the brace fix.

Example: test/storage.test.ts:362 'OutputArtefact lifecycle > lists all outputs' expected listOutputs() to return 2, got 0.

Repro: cd ~/screenferry && npm run test

title: F7: Delta transfer and cross-session resume
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F7, grade L). Scope extended by user: must also cover restarting interrupted transfers.

Send only what the receiver does not already have.

## Why
Turns a 4 GB re-send into ~40 MB for the 'update an air-gapped machine' case,
plausibly the single most common real use.

## The unifying insight (from user feedback)
A partially-received file IS 'a file the receiver already has'. Delta transfer
and resume-after-interruption are the same mechanism at different granularity:
- resume: receiver has blocks {0..n}, needs the rest -> D22 bitmap
- delta:  receiver has an older version, needs the changed regions
Designing them together avoids two overlapping subsystems.

## First step
Make cross-session resume robust first (it is the special case): streamId is
derived deterministically from file content and size, so re-picking the same
file after a reload or a crash must reproduce the same streamId and let the
bitmap apply. Test interrupted-then-resumed transfers explicitly.

## Then
Rolling-hash content-defined chunking for the general delta case, with a way for
the receiver to communicate what it holds (the section 6.2 repair code
generalises to this).

## Surviving objection -- MUST be resolved in the plan, not in code
Content-defined chunking tensions with D15 (fragment length L fixed) and D19
(fixed 4 MB blocks). Variable-length chunks break the 'K is derived, never
transmitted' property. Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme, or
resolve the tension explicitly before implementing.

Plan refs: D15, D19, D22, section 6.2, section 6.3. Phase 4+.

title: Resolve the I5 contradiction (concurrent manifest GE context)
description:
plan.md ref: I5 vs §7.6. I5: "Exactly one block is GE-active at a time", enforced by
"session type permits one active". The manifest needs its own GE context running
concurrently with a payload block, and RecvSession.active is a single nullable
field. Either amend I5 to permit a manifest context explicitly, or serialise
manifest acquisition — and say which.

title: Genesis: screenferry Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Static web app that ferries a file device-to-device across the screen-to-camera optical channel. No server, no network between devices, works offline. Must handle multi-gigabyte files with constant memory.

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0: Repo and harness
- [ ] Phase 1: Core codec, headless (fountain + GE + block layer)
- [ ] Phase 2: Single-QR optical loop
- [ ] Phase 3: Tiling and the profile ladder
- [ ] Phase 4: Large-file machinery (streaming, OPFS, resume, repair)
- [ ] Phase 5: The app (PWA, file I/O, coaching UI)
- [ ] Phase 6: Calibration probe + colour
- [ ] Phase 7: Custom codec (libcimbar-derived)

title: Persist the manifest for resume
description:
plan.md ref: §8.3, §7.6. §8.3 never says the manifest is persisted, so resume cannot
re-verify without re-acquiring it. Worse: at the beacon's ~2 s cadence a 4 GB
manifest takes ~12 minutes to acquire, and during that window no block can be
marked complete — so a reload loses EVERY received block, because the bitmap (the
resume token) is empty by §7.6's own rule. Persist the manifest alongside the
bitmap and state the pre-manifest reload behaviour.

title: Verify out-of-order block writes pass all hash checks
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Test that blocks arriving out of order write to correct positions
- Verify per-block hashes pass during out-of-order writes
- Confirm whole-file hash passes after completion (not scrambled)

## Context
This is the verification phase. We need to prove the fix works: simulate out-of-order block delivery and verify the file isn't scrambled, and both per-block and final whole-file hash checks pass.

title: Phase 6: calibration probe and colour
description:
plan.md ref: §17, D11. Ship the probe first
and let it settle luma-vs-colour. Note: on a decode-CPU-bound receiver RGB-stacked
QR triples the bits AND the decode work — a win when pixel-limited, a wash when
CPU-limited. Gate on the worker pool landing.

title: Reconcile the whole-file hash across three contradictory statements
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2 ("MANDATORY"), §3.3 ("optional"), §7.4 ("is optional"). Two of three were
not updated when it was made mandatory. concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact
reconstruction non-negotiable and names this as the verification.

title: npm run gate is red: 143 tsc errors across 15 files
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 while provisioning bench as screenferry owner.

npm run gate = typecheck && test && gate:numbers. The typecheck leg fails with 143 errors. It was previously masked by a syntax error (TS1128) at test/storage.test.ts:298, fixed in d3f4cbd; removing it unmasked the real backlog.

Worst files:
  51  test/deletion-integration.test.ts
  20  src/core/frame/beacon.ts
  13  src/platform/ge-benchmark.ts
  11  src/workers/ge-benchmark.worker.ts
  11  src/core/session/types.ts

Dominant codes: TS2339 property-does-not-exist (55), TS2532 object-possibly-undefined (43), TS2322 not-assignable (15).

The TS2339 cluster in test/deletion-integration.test.ts plus the ReceivingState/CompleteState 'writtenBlocks is missing' and IdleState errors in src/core/session/types.ts suggest the session state model drifted from what tests and callers expect. Reconcile the type model first, then the object-possibly-undefined cluster in beacon.ts.

Repro: cd ~/screenferry && npx tsc --noEmit

title: Phase 4: large-file machinery
description:
plan.md ref: §17. Streaming I/O, OPFS staging, quota
pre-flight, resume, the repair code, time estimation. Exit: A5, A6, A7, A10.

title: A/B the exposureCompensation lever
description:
plan.md ref: D14. Confirmed present and applied on the Pixel 6, but its effect size has never
been isolated.

title: Distance sweep to locate the camera px/module cliff
description:
plan.md ref: S3, spike/README.md. S3 bracketed it between 1.5 (100% erasure) and 4.5, but on
a heating device with one trial per point. Re-run under §13.2 conditions: tripod,
~300 lux, measured distance, >= 5 trials, median reported, cool start.

title: Specify the block-switch policy
description:
plan.md ref: I5, §8.1, §6.4. I5 mandates one active block and never says when to switch.
Camera frames straddle every transition, so packets for block n+1 arrive while n is
active. Switching on first sight of a higher blockIndex discards a 95%-complete
block, which then waits a full pass — hours. Propose: hold until rank K or M
consecutive higher-index packets (state M); consider permitting two concurrent
blocks during the overlap, since a second 264 KB working set still fits I6a.

title: Precache the zxing WASM locally
description:
plan.md ref: §6.5, T5, T7, A8. VERIFIED in the installed package: zxing-wasm@1.2.11 hard-codes
a fastly.jsdelivr URL and fetches the .wasm LAZILY ON FIRST DECODE. Shipping the
default gives a receiver that makes a third-party network request mid-session
(voiding T7, concept.md constraint 1 and the README's "provably no exfiltration"),
FAILS COMPLETELY IN AIRPLANE MODE (A8 — the flagship air-gapped case), and executes
remotely-fetched WASM (T5's surface). Fix with setZXingModuleOverrides({locateFile})
pointing at a service-worker-precached local .wasm.

title: Investigate compression/resume/T4-reap interaction and document failure modes
description:
## Task
Investigate and document the exact interaction between compression, resume functionality, and T4 privacy reaping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Document the current stateless sender assumption in §8.3
- [ ] Test CompressionStream output determinism across multiple runs
- [ ] Document the exact failure chain: restart → staging reaped → re-compress → different bytes → different hashes → silent invalid state
- [ ] Identify all code paths affected (sender, receiver, manifest, bitmap)
- [ ] Create a minimal reproduction case showing the hash divergence
- [ ] Document findings in a note under docs/notes/

## Dependencies
None (this is the first investigative step)

title: Add validation and tests for compression/resume fix
description:
## Task
Add comprehensive validation and test coverage for the compression/resume conflict fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add unit test for CompressionStream determinism (or lack thereof)
- [ ] Add integration test: sender restart with compression enabled
- [ ] Add test for the chosen fix (staging preservation OR resume prohibition)
- [ ] Verify no silent invalid state occurs after fix
- [ ] Add regression test covering the original failure chain
- [ ] All tests pass locally

## Dependencies
Depends on bf-vgtq (implementation must be complete first)

title: Add warning before keeping partial receiver artefacts
description:
Implement a user-visible warning when the receiver would keep a partial artefact instead of deleting it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Before keeping a partial artefact (e.g., on navigation away before completion), show a warning dialog
- Warning explains the security implication (plaintext data persists)
- User can choose to continue keeping the file or cancel/go back
- Warning is dismissable but shows the security context
- Warning is only shown when the artefact is genuinely partial, not after successful completion

## Implementation Notes
- Detect partial artefact state (incomplete download/decode)
- Trigger warning on navigation/close events
- Design clear, security-focused warning message
- Provide user action options (Keep / Cancel / Delete)

title: EPIC: fix the completion arithmetic
description:
The dwell cliff and D27 both make transfers that never finish. Verified
arithmetic. This is the finding most likely to sink the project quietly.

title: Add CRC-32 over the beacon body
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, review-3 critical #4. A corrupted beacon byte is caught by NOTHING beyond
T1's range checks. A corrupted blockCount gives a geometry that never completes.
§7.2 says the receiver shows "acquiring..." until its FIRST beacon — first beacon
wins, unvalidated. Add a CRC-32 over the beacon body, validated before streamId is
locked. Consider also requiring N identical beacons before locking.

title: Add positional write handle to RecvSession
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a new field for positional write handle in RecvSession class
- Keep existing sequential stream working unchanged
- The positional handle should be optional/nullable initially
- Type signature should match the new positional write interface

## Context
This is the first step: introduce the new positional write handle type alongside the existing out stream. Don't remove or change the existing stream yet — just add the new field so we can build on it.

title: Add deletion after successful share/save operations
description:
Implement automatic deletion of the receiver's decoded file after successful share() or save() operations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decoded file is deleted from browser storage after share() succeeds
- Decoded file is deleted from browser storage after save() succeeds  
- Deletion only occurs after the operation completes successfully
- Failed share/save operations do not delete the file
- Deletion is logged or visible in debugging UI

## Implementation Notes
- Hook into the share()/save() promise resolution
- Use the browser File System Access API or similar cleanup mechanism
- Ensure deletion is atomic with the operation success
- Add telemetry/debug logging for verification
close_reason: Already fully implemented in commit deab8a0 (src/platform/export.ts: shareFile/saveFile delete from OPFS after successful export, retain on failure/cancel, console logging). Bead was orphaned by the known NEEDLE 'agent exited successfully but bead still open' bug — agent completed and committed at 06:49:45 but never called bf close, so the fleet re-claimed it 4x and timed out each time trying to redo already-done work. Verified against all 5 acceptance criteria, all met.

title: Decide the dwell strategy against 48% measured erasure
description:
plan.md ref: §8.1, D18c, R12. spike-results.md measured 48% erasure in the one D9-compliant
run — above the 35.6% cliff. R12's mitigation does not address it: §8.2's repair
code retransmits at the SAME dwell and hits the same cliff, and D18a means nothing
in v1 can observe erasure to know to raise it.
OPTIONS: dwell 2.0 K (e_max 48.5%) at +98% standing overhead, which HALVES every
§13.1 figure and requires recomputing §1.1's hours-to-days table; or user-adjustable
dwell with a visible blocks-per-minute readout, giving the user the observable D18a
denies the software.

title: Fix the G1-G7 cadence contradiction in §14.6
description:
plan.md ref: §14.5 vs §14.6. §14.6 requires "G1-G5 green on one commit", contradicting
§14.5's "G5 is nightly, gates the nightly build", and omitting G7 which §14.5
singles out as same-commit mandatory.

title: Rung sweep R1 through R4
description:
plan.md ref: spike/README.md. Does the conservative rung decode where the aggressive one
fails? Kill criterion: if R1 fails while R3 works, §3.1.1's ladder needs
re-deriving.

title: Phase 5: the app shell and coaching UI
description:
plan.md ref: §17. PWA, service worker,
offline, file I/O per platform, wake lock, coaching UI, the no-back-channel progress
model, D18b's local adaptation. Resolve §19 Q4 and Q5 — both are v1 behaviour this
phase cannot ship without, and both are un-owned. Exit: A8, A9; every §11 code
reachable; iOS manual pass.

title: Specify the session state machine
description:
plan.md ref: §3.3, §7.3. Carried from two reviews. §7.3 gives state SHAPE but no transitions,
which are specified only as scattered edge cases: E8, E9, E10, E12, E16, D22 resume,
§8.3 re-verify, the "acquiring..." gate, §7.6's "verifying..." state and now D27's
duty cycle. At least ten states and a dozen transitions, defined nowhere as a unit.
streamId: number|null and meta: BeaconMeta|null are doing state-machine work through
nullable fields — the shape that produces forgotten-transition bugs.

title: Give D27's resolution lever a floor at 4 camera px/module
description:
plan.md ref: D27 vs S3. D27 says "drop decode resolution before dropping frames
(superlinearly cheaper)". S3 contradicts it: the Pixel 6 at 1080p was ALREADY at
2.25 camera px/module, below the cliff, and 720p measured 100% erasure with every
frame empty. There is no resolution headroom to surrender.

title: Document tools/ as retained infrastructure
description:
plan.md ref: §14.1, §16.2. tools/devrig.sh and tools/cdp_eval.py drive the two-device rig and
are the only way §13.1's optical budgets will ever be measured — the T-physical-rig
tier. The plan never mentions them, and spike/README.md says the spike directory is
deleted once results land. Also record vite.config.ts's HTTPS-via-tailscale-cert
requirement, a real onboarding constraint absent from §16.2.

title: Add payloadLen to the beacon
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2 vs D21, review-3 critical #3. D21 states payloadLen was moved INTO the
beacon; §7.2's field table does not have it. §7.2 claims blockSize + blockCount
"yields K and the last block's short length" — they CANNOT; blockCount*blockSize is
an upper bound. The receiver therefore cannot compute blockK(last), so the last
block's PRNG index sets mismatch and it never decodes with nothing saying why —
verbatim the failure E3a exists to prevent.

title: Build the minimal app shell so npm run build passes
description:
plan.md ref: §17. npm run build FAILS — no index.html, no src/app.ts. No deploy config, no
PWA manifest, no service worker.

title: Re-derive A4's occlusion parameters so the scenario is passable
description:
plan.md ref: §9 A4. A4 occludes the camera 30% of the time ON TOP OF baseline erasure; total
>= 37% means zero blocks ever complete, so it is currently unpassable. Its pass
criterion ("<= 1.6x the A1 frame count") also has no achievable middle — a missed
block costs a full pass, so the outcome is ~1.0x or >= 2x, never 1.6x.

title: Bound D26's sender-side K override at K_max and tie it to I6a
description:
plan.md ref: D26, I6a. D26 says a sender-side setting "MAY raise K when the user knows the
receiver is a desktop" with no upper bound. K=2048 gives a 512 KB matrix + 512 KB
block before recover() allocates its own K*L output — breaching I6a's 1 MB.

title: Design solution approach for compression determinism conflict
description:
## Task
Based on investigation findings from bf-2vke, design and evaluate solution approaches for the compression/resume conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Evaluate Option A: Preserve staging files across restarts (amend T4 to allow exceptional preservation)
- [ ] Evaluate Option B: Forbid resume when compression is enabled (detect and fail-fast)
- [ ] Evaluate Option C: Use deterministic compression (if feasible with CompressionStream)
- [ ] Document trade-offs for each option (privacy vs. correctness vs. complexity)
- [ ] Choose the recommended approach with rationale
- [ ] Document decision in docs/notes/ with implementation outline

## Dependencies
Depends on bf-2vke (investigation must be complete first)

title: Specify how receiver and sender thermal throttling are told apart
description:
plan.md ref: R11, E17a, E17b. The proxy — "sustained fps decline > 30% from a cool start" —
cannot distinguish them, and E17a records the SENDER decaying 6.7 -> 2.4 fps (-64%)
in two minutes. A receiver that duty-cycles in response to a sender thermal problem
makes it strictly worse.

title: Phase 7: custom grid codec
description:
plan.md ref: §17, §19 Q1, R7. RE-URGENTISED: at a
decodable cell size libcimbar is 0.0741 bits/screen px2 against QR v16-L @ 4px's
0.0447 — ~1.66x DENSER, not less dense as a retracted revision claimed. Blocked on
the MPL-2.0 licensing decision.

title: Audit current RecvSession.out type and §6.2 OPFS requirements
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Document current RecvSession.out type and its API characteristics
- Extract §6.2 requirements for worker-side OPFS handle (createSyncAccessHandle)
- Identify the mismatch: sequential stream vs. positional writes needed for out-of-order resume

## Context
§7.3's FileSystemWritableFileStream is async/sequential (main-thread). §6.2 uses createSyncAccessHandle (worker) with write(buf, {at}) for positional writes. With repair/resume, blocks arrive out of order — a sequential stream scrambles the file.

title: Extend G7's coverage past nine string matches
description:
plan.md ref: §14.5. G7 greps for nine formatted values. It cannot see §7.6's manifest
arithmetic, §6.3.2's tile counts or §8.1's dwell table — and the "working set
264.0 KB" figure it DOES pin is wrong once the manifest and recover()'s second K*L
array are counted (~650 KB, still inside I6a). The gate designed to keep numbers
honest is enforcing a stale one.

title: Add a lint config and wire it into G1
description:
plan.md ref: §14.5. There is NO lint config, so G1 ("typecheck, lint, unit, property,
stub-camera") cannot pass as written.

title: Implement block position tracking for RecvSession writes
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Add position tracking logic to RecvSession
- Track current block position as blocks are written
- Ensure position increments correctly for each block write
- Position should be queryable and updatable

## Context
Positional writes need accurate block position tracking. Implement the tracking logic that will be used by the positional write interface.

## Dependencies
This depends on having the positional write handle field in place.

title: Phase 3: tiling and the fixed-weight ladder
description:
plan.md ref: §17. Exit: A1 >= 20 KB/s,
A2, A3, A4 on the physical rig.

title: Enforce §16.3's version refusal in readPacket
description:
plan.md ref: §16.3 vs header.ts:57. §16.3 says a receiver seeing an unknown version "MUST
report E-VERSION ... and refuse — never attempt a partial parse". readPacket()
returns wireVersion and never refuses. Nothing in the parse path enforces it.

title: Add the rule: new sections must wire into their dependents
description:
plan.md ref: §14.6, §17.2. Three consecutive reviews found the same pattern: every critical
finding was in material added in the preceding commits, each time because a new
section's internal logic was sound but was never wired back into the sections it
depends on. §7.6 names eleven dependents and is referenced by one line. D27 was
never checked against §8.1. §7.2's mandatory hash left "optional" standing in two
places. §17.2 already has the symmetric rule for measurements — add this one.

title: Render the version footer (semver + build hash)
description:
plan.md ref: §17, bf-13h. Phase 0's exit requires it and it does not exist. It is also the
anchor for the whole verifiable-build story.

title: Define the fixed ladder weights
description:
plan.md ref: D18a, §17 Phase 3. D18a commits Phase 3 to "fixed weights" and the exit criterion
is named for it, but THE WEIGHTS ARE NEVER GIVEN. How many of ~15 tiles are
R1/R2/R3/R4 is the single number that determines Phase 3's throughput.

title: F1: Storage pre-flight and capacity gate
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F1, grade S).

Query navigator.storage.estimate() BEFORE accepting a file, and refuse or warn
immediately rather than failing mid-transfer.

## Why
The worst failure this app can have is discovering at hour 9 of a 10-hour
transfer that OPFS is full. Quotas differ sharply by platform:
- Chrome/Edge desktop: ~60% of free disk (multi-GB fine)
- Firefox: ~10% of disk, capped ~10 GB
- Safari/iOS: ~1 GB before prompting

## First step
Gate the file picker on estimated quota vs (file size + compression staging).
Refuse clearly, with the number, before anything starts.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- Verify per-block hashes on resume rather than trusting the bitmap
- Graceful stop on quota exhaustion: save what completed plus a manifest of
  what is missing

## Surviving objection
Quota APIs are advisory and Safari's is unreliable, so this can give false
confidence. Treat the estimate as a floor, not a guarantee, and still handle
mid-transfer exhaustion.

Plan refs: D19, D20, D22, open question 9. Phase 4.

title: Sweep cross-references, numbering and stale figures
description:
plan.md ref: Various. §7.6 sits between §7.2 and §7.3; §17.2 precedes §17.1; §18.1/§18.2 are
## where §17.1/§17.2 are ###; R11 after R12. "blocks per 4 GB" is 21,845 / 21,800 /
21,846 in different places. §3.1 still calls the 200 MB/s budget unmeasured. l.452
cites §16.3 for a §6.5 requirement. "(D-modulation-swappable)" is not a real ID.
§7.5 mixes base36 and Crockford base32, and §8.2's example is a character short.
E1/E4/E16/E18 have no error codes. I6a's "264 KB" understates by 2.5x. §13.1's
"refuse above 24 h" refuses §1.1's own headline case and does not say per-session or
total. §8.4 has no Android Chrome row though §13.2 names it the reference receiver.
spike-results.md still asserts the retracted "QR is denser than libcimbar" claim.

title: Rewrite D27 as block-granular duty cycling
description:
plan.md ref: D27, review-3 critical #6. VERIFIED: frame-granular 50% duty on 25% erasure
gives 0.5*0.75 = 0.375 delivered; dwell 1.6 yields 0.60 K against 1.03 K needed. So
D27's claim that duty cycling "FINISHES where 100% duty may not" is FALSE under the
plan's own model — it converts a slow transfer into one that never completes.
FIX: block-granular. The receiver knows blockIndex from the header, so it decodes
block N at full attention and skips N+1 entirely — doubling passes rather than
destroying every pass.

title: Build the GE benchmark component §16.4 owns
description:
plan.md ref: D26, T1, §16.4. D26 says the receiver "MUST refuse a stream whose K exceeds what
it benchmarked locally" and T1 makes that a security control. No such component
exists — §16.4's health check lists storage, camera, wake lock, OPFS write and the
calibration probe. Specify duration, K, a cached result keyed to device/UA, the
derived K_max, an error code for the refusal, and the recovery (the fix is on the
OTHER device, with no back-channel to request it).

title: Generalise the WASM rule to every dependency
description:
plan.md ref: §6.5, G3, §14.4. §6.5's warning is zxing-specific. Make it a rule: EVERY WASM
dependency must be bundle-local, SRI-pinned and exercised by §14.4's assertion. This
applies immediately to the incremental hasher the mandatory whole-file hash needs,
which is absent from §6.5's pin table and module tree.

title: Add a module-to-phase map
description:
plan.md ref: §6.5, §17. The five unwritten core modules (beacon.ts, repair-code.ts,
hash/block-hash.ts, hash/stream-id.ts, block/schedule.ts) have no phase owner.

title: F8: Pairing splash QR
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F8, grade S).

The sender displays a large QR containing the app URL so the receiver can load
the same page without being told where to go.

## Why
Solves a bootstrap problem nothing else in the plan addresses: 'we both need
the same page open' is the first thing that happens and currently has no answer.

## First step
Render the URL QR on the sender's idle/setup screen, before transmission starts.
Include a deep-link fragment so the receiver lands directly in receive mode.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- shareable deep links (/#recv)
- one-tap role inference: camera opens by default, dropping a file switches to
  send

## Surviving objection
An offline or air-gapped receiver cannot load a URL -- which is precisely the
scenario the app exists for. This helps the common case (both devices online,
neither has the app yet), not the hard case. Pair it with F6-style offline
distribution guidance rather than presenting it as the answer.

Plan refs: D13, section 7.1. Phase 5.

title: Define what the whole-file hash covers
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, E15. Original file or decompressed reassembly? E15 (decompression fails,
keep the compressed artefact) leaves a case where the hash can never be evaluated
at all.

title: Update RecvSession to use positional write output
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Change RecvSession.out type from sequential stream to positional write handle
- Update all write sites to use write(buf, {at}) instead of stream writes
- Ensure block position tracking passes through to the output handle

## Context
RecvSession currently uses a sequential stream. This is the core change: switch to the new positional write interface so out-of-order blocks write to the correct positions.

title: Rewrite E2: repetition is derived per block, not signalled
description:
plan.md ref: E2 vs encoder.ts:34 / decoder.ts:53. The plan is wrong and the code is right.
E2 says repetition is "signalled by a flags bit in the beacon", but repetition is a
PER-BLOCK property — blockK() returns 1-7 for the last block of any file — so a
session-wide flag would force repetition on all 21,845 blocks or none. Both ends
derive it from blockK(g, blockIndex) < MIN_LT_K using the shared function E3a
already mandates. No signalling required.

title: EPIC: outstanding measurements
description:
Everything §13.2 would accept as a qualifying measurement. Nothing measured so
far qualifies — three of seven denominator parameters deviate, and every S2/S3
number was taken on a device heating throughout.

title: Remove sequential stream code from RecvSession
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Remove old sequential stream field from RecvSession
- Clean up any unused stream-related code
- Ensure all writes go through positional interface
- Verify no functional regressions

## Context
Final cleanup: remove the old sequential stream once all writes are converted to positional. This completes the migration.

title: Validate D27's duty-cycle economics by measurement
description:
plan.md ref: D27, R11. Re-run the thermal profile with block-granular duty cycling at 50% and
confirm the claim that it roughly halves heat for roughly half the rate — and, more
importantly, that it completes.

title: Fix RecvSession.out's type to match §6.2's worker ownership
description:
plan.md ref: §7.3 vs §6.2. Typed FileSystemWritableFileStream — the async SEQUENTIAL
main-thread API — while §6.2 assigns OPFS to a worker using createSyncAccessHandle,
whose API is write(buf, {at}). With the repair code and resume, blocks complete OUT
OF ORDER, which requires positional writes. A sequential stream would either buffer
(breaking I4/I6b) or write in arrival order, silently producing a scrambled file
that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours.

title: Define error codes and recovery documentation
description:
Define error codes for K-based refusal and document recovery process.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Define specific error code for K-exceeds-K_max refusal (e.g., ERR_EXCESSIVE_K, code 4XX)
- Document the error code in API/spec with description
- Document recovery process: fix is on the OTHER device (sender)
- Document that no back-channel exists to request re-benchmark
- Update user-facing error messages with recovery guidance
- Document the security model (why refusal is necessary per D26/T1)

## Scope
- Error code definition and documentation
- Recovery documentation
- User-facing error messaging
- No implementation changes (documentation only)

## Implementation Notes
- Error code should be machine-readable and user-friendly
- Recovery docs should explain that sender must reduce K or re-benchmark
- No back-channel means receiver cannot request sender to adjust
- This completes the GE benchmark component per §16.4

title: Implement device/UA keyed caching for benchmark results
description:
Add persistent caching for GE benchmark results keyed by device/UA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Benchmark results are cached with a composite key of device fingerprint + user agent
- Cache persists across sessions (OPFS or IndexedDB)
- Cache entries include: timestamp, duration, measured K, device/UA identifiers
- Cache lookup returns cached result if available for current device/UA
- Cache has reasonable TTL (e.g., 30 days) with expiry handling
- Falls back to running benchmark if cache miss/expired

## Scope
- Caching layer implementation only
- No refusal logic, no K_max derivation, no error codes
- Builds on the benchmark runner from child bead

## Implementation Notes
- Use OPFS for persistence (consistent with other storage)
- Device fingerprint can be simple (e.g., screen size, platform, browser vendor)
- Cache structure should be extensible for future metadata

title: Reconcile the packets-per-frame basis across the plan
description:
plan.md ref: §6.3.1, §6.3.2, D1, §13.1. Three sections silently assume different values:
§6.3.1 budgets "15 tiles x 15 fps = 225 packets/s" (1 packet/tile); §6.3.2 gives
"15 tiles, 8.6 KB/frame" (2 packets/tile, and that 8.6 KB is QR CAPACITY not
payload — payload is 7.5 KB, which also violates §13.2's user-visible-bytes rule);
D1 cites ~7.8 KB at v15. At 1 packet/tile the geometry yields 36 KB/s; at 2, 72 KB/s.
Every headline number depends on a parameter never stated.

title: EPIC: close Phase 0's gates
description:
§17.2 records that Phase 0's exit criteria are unmet and that Phases 0.5 and 1
were built on top — PIVOT-CAUSES PH-2 in real time. Either meet them or amend §17,
but do not leave a gate that reads green and is not.

title: Add E-MANIFEST-* codes and an E12 livelock detector
description:
plan.md ref: §11, E12. There is no error code for manifest failure, none for the §7.6
"verifying..." state, none for D26's K-refusal, and none for a repair-code range
exceeding the file. E12's retry loop has no termination condition — a block failing
against a corrupt manifest retries forever, silently.

title: Bound K_manifest in T1 and fuzz it in A10
description:
plan.md ref: §12 T1, §9 A10. T1 bounds L, K, blockCount and fileSize. K_manifest is DERIVED
from blockCount, so T1's own permitted maximum (16.7 M blocks) yields a 262,144-
fragment manifest and an 8.6 GB matrix — an unbounded DoS the threat model does not
cover. A10 fuzzes fileSize; nothing fuzzes this path.

title: Update plan.md and documentation to reflect compression/resume fix
description:
## Task
Update project documentation to reflect the architectural decision and implementation for the compression/resume conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Update plan.md §8.3 to correct the stateless sender assumption
- [ ] Update T4 privacy section if staging preservation was chosen
- [ ] Update E11 reaping section if modified
- [ ] Document the constraint and its resolution in docs/notes/
- [ ] Update any relevant architecture diagrams or flow descriptions
- [ ] Cross-reference the implementation note from bf-3k90

## Dependencies
Depends on bf-2w1a (validation must be complete first)

title: Decide whether the beacon is a frame or a tile
description:
plan.md ref: §2, §7.2 vs §6.3, §7.1. §2 and §7.2 call it "a special FRAME carrying file-level
metadata instead of payload"; §6.3's diagram feeds it into the frame mixer and
§7.1's flags make it a packet type. These imply different sender loops, different
cadence overheads and different acquisition latency against §13.1's <=3 s
time-to-first-packet budget.

title: EPIC: specification debt
description:
Items a developer would otherwise have to invent, plus contradictions carried
across multiple reviews.

title: Implement the tight quad ROI with AP2's ratchet guard
description:
plan.md ref: §6.4, AP2. Worth 8.6x (56.9 -> 6.6 ms) when the code occupies part of the frame,
and nothing once the grid fills it — but load-bearing again at high capture
resolution, where a tight quad crop keeps camera px/module high AND pixel count
bounded. MUST implement AP2's guard: wide margin PLUS a forced full-frame rescan.
The first version was a one-way ratchet — 91% erasure, goodput worse than no
cropping, presenting as an optical fault. That guard currently exists only in
spike/rig.js, which the ground rules say to delete.

title: Re-spec the manifest as a fixed-K multi-block stream
description:
plan.md ref: §7.6, review-3 critical #1. VERIFIED: K_manifest = ceil(blockCount*4/L) grows
LINEARLY with file size — 342 fragments at 4 GB, 8,534 at 100 GB (8.7 MB matrix,
breaches I6a), 87,382 at 1 TB (910 MB matrix, unallocatable). §1.1 tables both as
in scope. This is AP3 verbatim, committed in the document that names AP3.

FIX: fixed K=768 manifest blocks;
blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount * blockHashLen / BLOCK), so it inherits the
flat-cost property. Use blockHashLen, not a hardcoded 4.

title: EPIC: the four throughput fixes Phase 3's gate rests on
description:
spike-results.md ranks these as worth ~10x between them, with no new decoder.
Best measured is 11.2 KB/s under non-qualifying conditions against a 20 KB/s gate
and a 10 KB/s kill criterion.

title: Implement D4's pinned QR mask and move encoding to a worker
description:
plan.md ref: D4, §6.3.1. Measured: 6.7 fps against 12 requested, decaying to 2.4 fps. D4
measured pinning as a 4.6-8x speedup — a bigger lever than library choice.
spike-results.md calls it "on the critical path, not an optimisation".

title: F2: Diagnostic stall detector
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F2, grade M).

When packets stop arriving, tell the user WHY, using metrics already computed.

## Why
4 px/module is a cliff, not a slope: below it zxing returns nothing at all, so
the app silently does nothing with no explanation. 'Fail-soft explanation' is
the difference between a usable tool and one people give up on.

## First step
A known-value canary tile in every frame. If the canary fails to decode, the
problem is optical, not payload -- that single signal cleanly separates the two
failure classes and anchors everything else.

## Also covers (absorbed 7 pool ideas)
- duplicate-frame detection (sender paused/asleep)
- wrong-streamId guard ('that is a different file', not silence)
- wake-lock failure warning before a multi-hour run dies at minute 3
- torn-frame rate surfacing (prompt to lower fps)
- autofocus-hunt detection
- dark-room / ambient conditions warning
- ETA that admits 'not converging at this distance'
- thermal/battery throttling detection

## Surviving objection
Misattributing a cause is worse than staying silent -- glare and distance can
present similarly. Prefer 'the code is not decodable, try moving closer' over a
confident wrong diagnosis.

Plan refs: D14, D18, section 4.3. Phase 5.

title: Run the GE benchmark on-device, including while throttled
description:
plan.md ref: §18.2, R1. spike/ge-bench.mjs runs unchanged in a browser. Desktop measured
3,260 MB/s; the /4 phone factor is an admitted guess. §18.2 says the condition that
matters is "sustained WHILE THERMALLY THROTTLED" — measure it there.
close_reason: Shipped in fc0a947 (GE benchmark thermal throttling test) plus notes/bf-5w1c.md. Bead stayed in_progress only because the worker prompt calls the missing br shim.

title: Design positional write interface matching createSyncAccessHandle API
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Design output handle interface with write(buf, {at}) method
- Ensure compatibility with worker-side OPFS createSyncAccessHandle semantics
- Interface must support out-of-order block writes without buffering

## Context
The new interface must mirror the worker's write(buf, {at}) capability: positional writes that don't depend on arrival order. This blocks complete out of order during repair/resume.

title: S4: phone-to-phone at 15 cm
description:
plan.md ref: R4, spike/README.md. Untested. §15 predicts ~54 cells against laptop->phone's
~165. Kill criterion: yields nothing at any rung -> document as a small-file-only
mode.

title: Add unit tests for deletion after successful share operations
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Test that shareFile() calls deleteOutput() after successful share
- Test that shareFile() does NOT call deleteOutput() when share fails
- Test that shareFile() does NOT call deleteOutput() when user cancels
- Mock navigator.share to simulate success, failure, and cancellation
- Verify storage.deleteOutput() is called/not called appropriately
- Test that deletion errors don't cause shareFile() to fail (graceful degradation)

## Scope
Add unit tests for the share operation deletion logic only. Do not modify the export.ts implementation - just add tests to verify it works correctly.

title: Add receiver orientation coaching (E-ORIENTATION)
description:
plan.md ref: §6.3.2, §11, bf-1g0. The spike's top-ranked improvement: holding the receiver in
landscape is 1.78x, free, and does NOT require halving screen px/module the way the
sender-side portrait region does. Verified negative: forcing the OS orientation does
not work — sensor mapping follows the device body. So this is coaching, not
configuration.

title: Add a long-run tier to §14.1 and a duration budget to §13.1
description:
plan.md ref: §13.2, §14.1, R11. §13.2 specifies "Duration: >= 60 s sustained", so BY
CONSTRUCTION no qualifying measurement can observe a phenomenon that takes 20-30
minutes to appear. R11 is the highest-rated risk in the register and is currently
structurally unmeasurable.

title: F4: Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1)
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F4, grade S). Entered via the gap round.

A full-screen, high-contrast, rapidly-changing animation is a genuine
photosensitive-seizure risk. WCAG 2.3.1 requires no more than three general
flashes per second, or keeping flashing area below the small-safe threshold.

## Why
The QR research flagged this explicitly and it is an obligation rather than a
preference. The app flashes high-contrast frames at 12-15 fps, potentially
full-bleed, for hours.

## First step
Do not render full-bleed. Keep the coded area inside a bounded region with a
static surround, which is also the cheapest route to compliance. Add a
reduced-motion mode honouring prefers-reduced-motion, and warn before starting.

## The tension worth surfacing
The mitigation directly costs the core metric -- bounding flash area reduces
usable screen area, which reduces cells, which reduces throughput. This is a
real tradeoff to measure, not a checkbox. Quantify the cost in Phase 3 so the
decision is informed.

Plan refs: D10 (DC balance already helps), D12. Phase 5.

title: Add unit tests for deletion after successful save operations
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Test that saveFile() calls deleteOutput() after successful save
- Test that saveFile() does NOT call deleteOutput() when save fails  
- Test that saveFile() does NOT call deleteOutput() when user cancels
- Mock showSaveFilePicker to simulate success, failure, and cancellation
- Verify storage.deleteOutput() is called/not called appropriately
- Test that deletion errors don't cause saveFile() to fail (graceful degradation)

## Scope
Add unit tests for the save operation deletion logic only. Do not modify the export.ts implementation - just add tests to verify it works correctly.

## Dependencies
Depends on: bf-69cw (share deletion tests)

title: Define the beacon size bound and filename truncation
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, T2. Fixed fields total ~54 B against R1's 256 B payload, leaving ~200 B
for filename + mimeType + length prefixes. A 255-byte UTF-8 filename is legal on
every mainstream filesystem and overflows with no specified truncation or
fragmentation rule. T2 says only "cap length".

title: Document deletion lifecycle and troubleshooting
description:
## Acceptance Criteria  
- Update or create documentation explaining the deletion lifecycle
- Document when files are deleted vs retained
- Document how to verify deletion is working in production
- Add troubleshooting section for common deletion issues
- Include examples of log output showing successful/failed deletion
- Document how to manually clean up OPFS if automatic deletion fails

## Scope
Create comprehensive documentation for the deletion feature that helps users understand when files are cleaned up and how to troubleshoot if automatic deletion isn't working.

## Dependencies
Depends on: bf-1qi9 (enhanced logging)

title: Add integration test for end-to-end deletion workflow
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Test complete workflow: write output → export → verify deletion
- Test that OPFS file is actually removed after successful export
- Test that OPFS file persists after failed/cancelled export
- Test with real OPFS storage (not mocked)
- Verify manifest is updated correctly after deletion
- Test reaping of orphans still works after export deletions

## Scope
Add integration test that verifies the complete deletion workflow works end-to-end with real OPFS storage. This confirms the unit tests and implementation work together correctly.

## Dependencies
Depends on: bf-6dho (save deletion tests)

title: Implement positional write output handle for worker OPFS
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Implement the output handle with write(buf, {at}) method
- Handle must integrate with worker-side OPFS createSyncAccessHandle
- Must support concurrent out-of-order writes without buffering blocks

## Context
This is the implementation phase: we need a handle that can write to specific positions in the file, matching the semantics of createSyncAccessHandle's write(buf, {at}).

title: Resolve the I9 contradiction (write-before-verify)
description:
plan.md ref: I9 vs §7.6. I9: "A block MUST NOT be written to OPFS until its hash verifies",
enforced by a mandated test. §7.6: blocks are "written to OPFS but not marked in
the bitmap; verified retroactively". Direct contradiction of a MUST.

Decide: amend I9 to "written but unverified, never surfaced", or require the
manifest before any OPFS write. Note retroactive verification means re-reading and
re-hashing every written block — a full extra pass, currently unbudgeted — and that
E12's "clear its bitmap bit" is a no-op for blocks whose bit was never set.

title: Add GE benchmark runner to health check suite
description:
Create the GE benchmark component that measures stream processing capability.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Add a new benchmark runner to the existing health check suite (alongside storage, camera, wake lock, OPFS write, calibration probe)
- The benchmark runs a configurable duration and returns a measured K value
- Integrates with the existing health check infrastructure
- Returns a structured result with duration and K metrics
- Fails gracefully if the benchmark cannot run

## Scope
- Benchmark runner implementation only
- Integration with health check suite
- No caching, no refusal logic, no error codes

## Implementation Notes
- Follow the pattern of existing health check components
- Configurable duration (start with a reasonable default)
- Returns raw K value (not yet cached)

title: Implement startup cleanup of orphaned receiver outputs
description:
Add automatic cleanup of orphaned decoded files when the receiver app starts up.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On app startup, scan for and identify orphaned output files
- Orphaned files are those that exist in browser storage without a corresponding active session
- Identified orphans are automatically deleted
- Cleanup runs in the background without blocking app initialization
- Cleanup results are logged (count of files cleaned up)

## Implementation Notes
- Add a startup worker/initialization hook
- Define 'orphan' criteria (e.g., files older than X hours without session reference)
- Use async cleanup to avoid blocking UI
- Add metrics/logging for verification

title: Carry the manifest's hash inside the beacon
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, §7.6. The block hashes now travel in a structure with no check of its own.
One flipped byte in a manifest packet yields wrong hashes for hundreds of blocks,
which then fail E12 forever — re-collect, fail, re-collect — with no error code and
no termination. The beacon already carries 32 bytes of hash; add 4-8 more for the
manifest. That roots the chain: beacon -> manifest -> blocks -> whole file.

title: Add K_max derivation and K-based stream refusal
description:
Implement K_max derivation from cached benchmark and add stream refusal logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Derives K_max from cached benchmark result with safety margin
- Adds stream K validation on receiver side (per D26 security control)
- Refuses stream if sender K exceeds locally benchmarked K_max
- Returns specific error code when K exceeds K_max
- Logs the refusal with context (sender K, local K_max, device/UA of benchmark)

## Scope
- K_max derivation logic
- Stream validation and refusal
- No caching implementation (uses cached result from child bead)
- No recovery documentation yet

## Implementation Notes
- K_max should be benchmark K with reasonable safety margin (e.g., 80-90%)
- Error code should be distinct from other stream errors
- D26 compliance: MUST refuse stream if K exceeds local benchmark

title: Create user-visible delete control for receiver files
description:
Add a user-accessible control to manually delete the receiver's decoded file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delete button is visible in the receiver UI (e.g., near the output display)
- Button is clearly labeled (e.g., 'Delete decoded file')
- Clicking deletes the file from browser storage
- Confirmation dialog or toast notification confirms deletion
- Delete control is disabled when no file exists
- Control is keyboard accessible

## Implementation Notes
- Add delete button to receiver UI component
- Wire up deletion handler to browser storage cleanup
- Add confirmation dialog to prevent accidental deletion
- Show success/error feedback after deletion
- Update button state based on file existence

title: Document the normative wire constants in §7
description:
plan.md ref: §7, §14.3. Fixed in code and absent from the plan: MAGIC=0x5, the CRC-8 poly
0x31 / init 0xff, the CRC-32 variant, SplitMix32's constants, packetSeed's mixing
order (the code says "Order is normative"), and the partial-Fisher-Yates index
derivation. §14.3 promises conformance vectors "because they are what a third-party
implementation would need" — a third party cannot currently write one.

title: Implement chosen solution for compression/resume conflict
description:
## Task
Implement the solution chosen in bf-3k90 for the compression/resume/T4-reap conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement the chosen approach (preserve staging OR forbid resume with compression OR deterministic compression)
- [ ] If preserving staging: modify T4 reaping logic with exception handling
- [ ] If forbidding resume: add detection and early error on sender start
- [ ] Update relevant code paths (sender initialization, staging cleanup)
- [ ] Ensure the fix prevents the silent invalid state failure mode
- [ ] Add inline comments explaining the constraint

## Dependencies
Depends on bf-3k90 (solution design must be complete first)

title: Split fileSize into payloadSize and originalSize
description:
plan.md ref: §7.2, T1, T3, D23, E3a. One field must currently mean three incompatible
things: E3a's block arithmetic needs the COMPRESSED length, while T1's quota check,
T3's decompression-bomb cap and D23's ETA need the ORIGINAL. If fileSize is the
compressed size, T3's bomb cap aborts every legitimately compressed transfer.

title: Define A1-lite as Phase 2's exit criterion
description:
plan.md ref: §17, §9 A1. §17 Phase 2 says "A1 passes at any speed", but A1's own pass criteria
include ">= 20 KB/s and completes in <= 60 s" with a fail at < 10 KB/s. A named
scenario cannot mean two things. Define A1-lite: byte-exactness on two real devices,
no throughput floor.

title: EPIC: close the wire format before Phase 2
description:
Every child is a one-way door under §16.3 — once shipped, changing it strands
cached receivers. Phase 2 is the first phase that writes a decoder, so all of this
must land first. Closes when all children close.

title: State whether the manifest inherits E2's repetition mode
description:
plan.md ref: §7.6, E2. K_manifest can fall below MIN_LT_K=8 on small files (a 50 MB file
gives 5 fragments at the old sizing), silently entering repetition mode. §7.6 does
not say whether the manifest inherits E2's rule.
